chapter: Rose Murphy, wartime 52nd Street, Town Hall
title: Chronology of the early 1950s: his own groups and the Goodman years
summary: Crouch reconstructs the sequence; between 1948 and 1955 Stewart freelanced and led groups with Billy Taylor, Beryl Booker and John Collins, after about two and a half years with Goodman from 1945.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Now, prior to the mid-'50s, do you recall who you were working with, say between 1950 and 1955?
Well, offhand, I'm not sure. I worked with quite a few little groups here and there. I had my own
group.
Oh, you were working with your own group too in the early '50s?
Oh yes, sure.
Who were you using?
Well, Billy Taylor was with me on one occasion (unintelligible) Billy Taylor.
Right.

And of course, Beryl Booker, John Collins on guitar -- Beryl Booker played the piano, of course -- and drummers. We used to use quite a few drummers. We'd mix it all up. I can't remember names too well.

But so like now, when you -- so you had -- so now after -- trying to get this chronology together. Now you had -- you worked -- what did you say? From about 1936 or so to about 1941, you worked with Slim Gaillard.
Slim Gaillard, yeah, right.
Then you worked for a bit, between Tatum and having your own band, with Erroll Garner.
Erroll Garner, yes.
And you went to Europe with Erroll Garner.
Went to Europe with Erroll Garner.
Did some freelancing, a lot of freelancing. You played with Charlie Parker and --
Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie, of course.
Those guys. Then you went to Europe in 1948.
Yes, yes.
Then when you came back from Europe, you also were working -- you say that you were working -- you were freelancing --
Freelance, yes.
-- and occasionally leading your own bands, including Billy Taylor --
That's right, yes.
-- Deryl Booker, John Collins and a variety of different drummers.
Right, that's right.
Okay, so now is this pattern that you had more or less, say, for seven years from say 1948 to about '55 or so, around in there.
That's about it. Of course, I --
Did you do any -- oh, go ahead.
Did I mention that between -- really, it was the year 1945 that I worked -- I joined Benny Goodman, I think I mentioned.
Yeah, we did talk about that.
That lasted -- the first time around
with him, that lasted about two and a half years.
Uh-huh. So about the time you ended up, finished with him, that -- shortly after that, you went to Europe and worked with Erroll Garner and that festival that PA-nassie did.
Yes, right. And I was, like you said, freelancing, you know, up until more or less after -- well, here and there, you might say.
